risk.statement: This is a high-risk feature. Your AI can be wrong and can change your network devices. You carry the risk yourself. Vedette is provided as is under the Apache-2.0 license; its author, Kien Nguyen, is not responsible for actions your AI takes.

page.title: Response
page.meta: Rules you build (WHEN, IF, THEN) and requests your AI sends. Every action needs approval by default, and nothing changes another device without the safety envelope below.
page.onBody: Actions that change your network devices can run after a person approves them. {{count}} request(s) waiting. Use Emergency stop if something looks wrong.
page.breakerTitle: Circuit breaker is open: all response is paused
page.breakerBody: More than {{max}} actions were requested in one hour, so rules and AI requests are paused and your channels were told.
page.stoppedBody: Someone pressed Emergency stop, so rules and AI requests are paused and no device step runs, an undo included, until an administrator resumes.

plans.title: Plans from the AI for critical findings
plans.description: For each unresolved critical finding the AI reads your inventory and your connections and proposes how to contain it. Nothing runs from here without an approval.
plans.emptyBody: When a device in your inventory has an unresolved critical finding, the AI drafts a plan here.
plans.noAi: The AI is not set up for response plans
plans.noAiBody: Assign an AI profile to the Response plan job to get plans.

blocked.execution_off: Execution is off. Turn it on in Settings, AI response (high risk).
blocked.tool_not_allowed: This action is not enabled. Enable it in Settings, AI response (high risk).
blocked.tool_unavailable: The connection or its write tool is turned off in Settings → Connections.
blocked.not_publishable: This blocks an address the block list never publishes (private or reserved), so it would do nothing. Use a device action to stop a device on your LAN.

requests.title: Requests
requests.description: One request per rule run or AI proposal. The approver can approve everything or pick actions. High-risk requests need two different approvers. A request expires after 15 to 30 minutes with nothing done, and a notice is sent.
requests.emptyBody: Requests appear here when a rule matches or the AI sends one.
requests.emptyPending: Nothing is waiting for a decision

action.approved: Approved. The action was carried out.
action.viaBox: Block list on this box (no connection needed)
action.links: Approval links that would be emailed
action.linksHint: Preview build only. On a real box each approver gets their own link by email. Opening a link shows the change and changes nothing: the approver must press a button on the page.

stop.done_one: Execution is off. {{count}} pending request cancelled.
stop.done_other: Execution is off. {{count}} pending requests cancelled.

panel.title: Response plan
panel.description: AI-drafted plan for this device, based on your inventory and connections.

settings.title: AI response (high risk)
settings.description: Allow Vedette to carry out changes on your network devices, only after the right people approve them. Actions that change only this box (block list, messages) do not need the switch; actions that change another device do. Execution is off by default.
settings.switch: Let the AI carry out actions I approve
settings.off: Off. The AI can propose but cannot change anything.

enable.title: Turn on AI execution
enable.description: Read this and confirm. You can turn it off at any time, and Emergency stop is always one click away.
enable.toAccount: Turn it on in My account

form.perHour: Maximum approved device actions per hour
form.expiryHint: 15 to 30. After that nothing happens and a notice is sent.
form.noChannels: No channel has approvals in chat turned on, so approvals happen in the app only.
form.channelsHint: Only channels with approvals turned on and at least one approver can be chosen. Each channel keeps its own approver list (Settings, Alert channels).
form.approversRule: A decision counts only if the sender is on that channel's approver list, is an operator or admin in Vedette, and proved that address themselves: in My account, or for Zalo by confirming, signed in to Vedette, the link sent to that Zalo account. No administrator can link an address for someone else. Several approvers are allowed; the first valid decision wins.
form.notLinkedYet: Not linked yet: {{names}}. Their buttons and links do not count until they link in My account.

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: WHEN something happens, IF the conditions hold, THEN run the actions you chose. New rules start in dry run: matches are logged and nothing runs until you switch the rule to live.
rules.dialogHint: Pick what to watch, how sure Vedette must be, what to do, and how.
rules.name: Name

triggers.ioc_connection: a device on your network connects to a known-bad IP address or domain
triggers.honeypot: a device touches a honeypot trap
triggers.nat_critical: a critical finding can be reached from the Internet through port forwarding (NAT)

rules.minConfidenceHint: Only matches at least this sure. Automatic mode needs 80 or more.
rules.feedsHint: Comma-separated feed names. Empty means any feed.
rules.assetTypesHint: Tick none to include every device.
rules.autoRefused: Automatic is only offered for IOC rules with a minimum confidence of 0.8 or more and an action that is not high risk.
rules.autoWarning: Automatic: Vedette acts without asking anyone. A wrong match can cut off something you need. The never-block list and the limits below still apply.
rules.ttlHint: The change is removed automatically after this time.
rules.perHourHint: More matches than this are refused and logged.
rules.safeguards: Removed after {{ttl}} minutes, at most {{n}} per hour.
rules.safetyNote: Never-touch list, circuit breaker, maintenance windows and limits apply to every rule.
rules.liveBody: From now on a match creates a real request. Actions still need approval unless the rule is pre-approved.
rules.dryTitle: Switch this rule back to dry run?
rules.dryBody: Matches will only be logged. Nothing will be requested or run.
rules.dryNote: Dry run: matches are written to the log only. Use Simulate to see the exact commands.
rules.deleteBody: The rule stops at once and cannot be brought back. Its log entries and past requests are kept.

det.title: Recent events
det.description: What the triggers watch for: honeypot touches, known-bad connections, findings, unknown devices, log thresholds and new ports.
det.ran: {{matched}} new match(es): {{dry_run}} dry run, {{requests}} request(s), {{executed}} done by pre-approval, {{deduped}} merged, {{refused}} refused.
det.previewNote: Preview build: events are sample data and you press Check now. On a real box the rules run continuously.
det.descriptionNoTraps: What the triggers watch for: known-bad connections, findings, unknown devices, log thresholds and new ports.

allow.title: Never-touch list
allow.description: Addresses no rule or AI request may ever change: the gateway, DNS servers, domain controllers, this box and management IPs. A match cancels the run and is logged.
allow.empty: The list is empty. Add your gateway and DNS servers before turning any rule on.
allow.valueHint: IP address, range like 192.168.10.0/24, or a domain.
allow.label: What it is

blocklist.title: Block list for your firewall
blocklist.description: The preferred way: your firewall fetches a list from this box. No write access to the firewall is given to Vedette.
blocklist.pull: Pull: the firewall fetches the list from this address every few minutes. It needs no credentials for Vedette and Vedette holds none for the firewall. The token in the address is the only credential, so keep the address inside your LAN.
blocklist.emptyWhat: Only approved "block" actions add addresses here: a rule or an AI request that adds an address to the block list, once a person approves it or a pre-approved rule runs.
blocklist.emptyPublic: Only public addresses are published. A block on a private or reserved address (192.168.x, 10.x, 100.64.x and the like) is refused when it is planned, and the Response log says why.
blocklist.emptyTemplate: The ready-made rule "Known-bad connection: add the destination to the block list" ships switched off.
blocklist.emptyLink: Turn it on: Rules, Template gallery
blocklist.ipOnly: The list holds public IP addresses only, one per line. Its first three lines start with # and name only the list, the time and the number of entries. Expired entries drop out by themselves.
blocklist.setupDescription: Pick your firewall and follow the steps. The address above is already filled in.
blocklist.pushBody: When the firewall cannot fetch a list, Vedette can change it through an API or SSH connection (Settings → Connections) with the action Block an IP address on the office firewall. Push needs a write credential on the firewall, so it needs your approval each time unless you set the rule to automatic.
blocklist.regenerateBody: The current address stops working at once. Update the address on your firewall afterwards, or it will keep an old list.

log.title: Response log
log.description: Every rule match, proposal, request, decision, execution, rollback, removal and refusal. Each line carries the hash of the line before it, so editing or deleting a line is detected.
log.emptyBody: Steps appear here as rules and requests run.

catalog.title: Action catalog
catalog.hint: Template packs (action templates are data you can edit) and generic actions in plain words. An action is allowed when it is switched on. Rules can only use switched-on actions, and the AI only those you also flag "AI may propose".
catalog.boxOnly: Changes nothing on another device. No connection needed.
catalog.dialogHint: Describe what the action does, choose the connection, and give the exact command or API call with a way to undo it. The fields follow the kind of the connection.
catalog.name: Name
catalog.description: What it does, in plain words
catalog.descriptionHint: People read this when they approve. Up to 300 characters.
catalog.placeholders: Use only these placeholders, filled in by Vedette and checked first: {ip}, {cidr}, {domain}, {port}, {mac}, {vlan}, {interface}, {id} (whole number), {name} (letters, numbers, . _ -). Shell characters such as ; | & $ ` < > ( ) are refused.
catalog.commandHint: Optional if you give an API call.
catalog.pathHint: Under the connection address. Starts with /.
catalog.readOnly: Read-only: this connection has no write tools
catalog.needConnection: The connection you need is not listed? Add one first; typed text here is not kept.
catalog.noWritable: No connection has write tools yet. Turn on a write tool in Settings → Connections.
catalog.pickToolFirst: Pick the write tool of this connection that does this step.
catalog.verifyHint: How to read the result back after the action runs.
catalog.expectHint: After the action the read-back output must contain this text, and after the undo it must not. Typed placeholders such as {ip} are filled in. Leave it empty and the result is shown as "not checked": a call that answered OK is not proof the change is in place.
catalog.precheckHint: A read-only command or GET that runs right before the action. If its output contains one of the texts below, Vedette changes nothing. Needed for any action that uses {interface}, so a trunk or uplink port is never touched.
catalog.precheckNoMcp: An MCP server cannot run a check before yet.
catalog.precheckExpectHint: If the output does not contain this text, nothing is changed. Up to 80 plain characters, capital letters count. An empty output always refuses.
catalog.refuseHint: One text per line, up to {{max}}, each up to {{len}} characters, matched exactly (capital letters count). For example: Administrative Mode: trunk
catalog.checkedBefore: Checked before it runs. Refuses on: {{texts}}
catalog.expectOnlyReadBack: The text to look for belongs to the read-back only.
catalog.needsPrecheck: An action that names a port ({interface}) needs a check before it, with at least one text that makes it refuse, so a trunk or uplink port is never touched.
catalog.aiMayHint: The AI can send a request for this action. It never writes the command.

kinds.http: HTTP API connection: method, path, headers and body.
kinds.netconf-restconf: NETCONF / RESTCONF connection: method, path, headers and body.
kinds.automation: Automation platform connection: the job to start and its variables, as method, path, headers and body.
kinds.mcp-http: MCP server: pick one of its write tools and map its arguments.
kinds.mcp-stdio: MCP server: pick one of its write tools and map its arguments.

packs.generic: Generic: messages, webhooks and your own actions

catalog.placeholdersMessage: Use {text} (short plain text) for the message. Shell characters such as ; | & $ ` < > ( ) are refused.

approve.title: Approve a response action
approve.intro: {{name}}, Vedette asks you to decide on this change.
approve.once: It can be used once. Opening it does not approve anything.
approve.doneApprove: Approved. The action is being carried out. You can close this page.
approve.doneReject: Rejected. Nothing was changed. You can close this page.

state.expired: This link has expired. Ask for a new approval request.

approve.doneWaiting: Your approval was recorded. A second, different approver is needed before anything runs. You can close this page.
approve.twoNeeded: Approvals so far: {{n}} of {{of}} needed from different people.

request.noAutoUndo: Not undone automatically (undo it by hand)
request.unknown: The result of this change is unknown. Undo it to be sure it is not in force.
request.recorded: Approval {{n}} of {{of}} recorded. A second, different person must approve.
request.secondNeeded: {{name}} approved. A second, different approver must approve the same actions.
request.codeHint: High-risk AI requests are approved in the app only, with the 6-digit code from your two-step sign-in.
request.inAppOnly: High risk: only an in-app approval with your two-step code counts. A tap in chat or an emailed link is refused.

reject.title: Reject this request
reject.reasonAi: Optional. The AI will not ask again for 7 days unless it has new evidence.
reject.memory: Save as a memory hint for the AI
reject.rule: Save as a rule hint for the AI

editor.hint: Pick WHEN it starts, IF it applies, and THEN what to do. Every action needs approval unless you choose the pre-approved option.
editor.noConditions: No conditions: the rule applies to every event of this trigger.
editor.paramHint: A fixed value, or a trigger field written as double braces around trigger.field_name. It is checked by type before use.
editor.undoHint: The change is undone automatically after this time.
editor.verifies: After it runs, Vedette reads the result back to check it.
editor.attacker: Trigger data is attacker-controlled. A device name, log line or domain can be crafted to hurt you, so Vedette checks every value by type (IP address, range, domain, port, MAC, VLAN, interface, plain text), escapes it for where it goes, and refuses shell characters and line breaks. A value that fails the check cancels the whole run.
editor.approvalDefault: Actions run in this order. One bundled request is sent per run: the approver can approve all or pick actions. High-risk actions need two different approvers.
editor.preHint: Off by default. Admin only. Only for low-risk actions that can be undone within 24 hours.
editor.preAdmin: Only an admin can turn this on.
editor.preNotEligible: Not available: every action must be low risk, reversible and have an undo time of 24 hours or less.
editor.preWarning: Pre-approved: Vedette will carry out these actions without asking anyone. A wrong match can still block something you need. The never-touch list and the limits still apply.
editor.preBad: This rule cannot be pre-approved with these actions. The server refuses it.

types.id: whole number (for example a policy number)
types.name: name

editor.nameBad: Give a name of 1 to 80 letters, numbers, spaces and . , : ' ( ) / -
editor.scheduleBad: Run every 15 minutes to 7 days (10080 minutes).
editor.ttlBad: Give 5 minutes to 30 days (43200 minutes), or leave it empty.
editor.hourBad: Give a whole number from 1 to 100.

sim.title: Simulation
sim.approvals_one: A live run would need {{count}} approver.
sim.approvals_other: A live run would need {{count}} different approvers.

templates.title: Template gallery
templates.description: Ready-made rules, switched off and in dry run. Clone one, then edit it to fit your network.
templates.cloned: Cloned: switched off, in dry run
templates.notHere: Not available on this install: it needs internal traps, which this install cannot run.

safety.title: Safety envelope
safety.description: Enforced on the server for every rule and AI request. Duplicates of the same target and action are merged, each rule has its own hourly limit, and an emergency stop is always available.
safety.breakerHint: More than this pauses all rules and AI requests and notifies your channels.
safety.multi: Second approver above this many targets
safety.multiHint: An action that touches more targets than this needs two different approvers.
safety.windowsHint: No rule or AI request is created during a window.
safety.trippedBody: More than {{max}} actions in one hour, at {{time}}. Notified: {{who}}.
safety.stoppedBody: Emergency stop pressed at {{time}}. No step that touches a device runs, an undo included, until you resume.

aiGates.title: AI requests: gates
aiGates.description: The AI can only send a request for triggers you allow here, and only for actions you flagged "AI may propose". The server enforces every gate; the AI cannot talk its way around them.

fixed.1: It names a catalog action and typed values. It never writes commands.
fixed.2: It must point at real evidence (a finding, a known-bad connection, a connection read) that the server checks.
fixed.3: Confidence must be 0.8 or more. Below that it is a suggestion note with no approval request.
fixed.4: One open request per target and action. After a rejection, no repeat for 7 days unless there is new evidence.
fixed.5: Over budget, proposals go into a digest. If more than half of the last 10 were rejected, AI requests pause and the admin is told.
fixed.6: High risk adds a second checker and needs two approvers in the app with the two-step code.

metrics.title: Acceptance
metrics.description: How often people approve what rules and the AI ask for, and how fast.
metrics.rejectedDescription: Reasons help you tune rules and teach the AI what to leave alone.

ai.title: AI requests
ai.description: Confidence of {{conf}} or more, evidence the server can verify, and no repeat for {{days}} days after a rejection.
ai.pausedBody: More than half of the last 10 were rejected. Look at the reasons below, then resume.
ai.noHints: No hints saved. Reject an AI request with a reason to teach it.

try.title: Try an AI request (preview build)
try.description: Stands in for the AI agent. Send a request and see which server gate answers. Try the presets, then change the values.

identity.title: Approval channels
identity.desc: Buttons and email links from an approval channel count as you only after you prove that the address or ID an administrator saved for you is yours. Approving in the app always works.
identity.none: You are not an approver on any channel.
identity.linkedAt: Linked {{at}}. Buttons and links from this address count as you.
identity.howEmail: Send a code to this address and enter it here. It is your sign-in email; if it is wrong, ask an administrator to correct it.
identity.howSend: Your administrator listed this {{channel}} account as yours. When they save it, the Vedette {{channel}} account sends it a confirm link: open it and confirm while signed in to Vedette as yourself. Ask your administrator to press Send again if the link expired.
identity.howChat: Press Approve or Reject on the next approval message in {{channel}}. Nothing is decided: Vedette answers only you with a 6-digit code. Enter it here, then press the button again. Only enter a code that Vedette showed you after you pressed a button yourself; never one someone sent you.
identity.sent: Code sent to {{to}}. It expires in 10 minutes.
identity.unlinkedToast: {{channel}} unlinked. Its buttons and links no longer count as you.
identity.unavailable: {{channel}} cannot yet answer only you, so it cannot be linked. Its buttons do not count for you; approve in Vedette.
